questions.question: In a PLONKish circuit, what is the main purpose of a selector column?
options: Enable a gate on specific rows of the table
Store private witness values in advice columns
Provide public inputs to the verifier as instances
Choose random challenges for the prover transcript
questions.explanation: Selectors are fixed 0/1 values that multiply constraints so gates apply only on chosen rows.

questions.question: Conceptually, what does a copy constraint enforce?
options: Two specific cells must have equal values
All advice cells must be distinct values
A fixed column must be public to the verifier
The circuit must use only linear constraints
questions.explanation: A copy constraint ties two cells together so they represent the same logical variable across the table.

questions.question: Why do we multiply each gate constraint by the selector value in MockProver?
options: To disable the constraint when the selector is 0
To replace division constraints with multiplication
To convert fixed columns into advice columns
To force every constraint to hold on all rows
questions.explanation: Multiplying by a 0/1 selector makes constraints vacuously true when the gate is turned off.

questions.question: If a witness value is assigned but never referenced by any gate or copy constraint, what is it?
options: An unconstrained value (a free variable)
A public input value fixed by the verifier
A fixed constant value baked into circuit
A selector value used to enable a gate
questions.explanation: Unreferenced advice is unconstrained, so the prover can choose it arbitrarily without affecting satisfiability.

questions.question: In the 3-bit decomposition gate, which constraint forces d0 to be a bit?
questions.explanation: Over a field, x(x-1)=0 forces x to be either 0 or 1.

questions.question: Which soundness bug can an attacker exploit if a circuit forgets a needed copy constraint?
options: Use different values in two places that should match
Recover the field modulus from the public transcript
Compute prover randomness from the instance column
Replace a multiplication gate with an addition gate
questions.explanation: Without the equality, the prover can pick unrelated values for the two cells and still satisfy the remaining constraints.

questions.question: Which statement best describes an instance column?
options: It holds public values that the verifier fixes
It stores intermediate witness values for gates
It is a selector column that turns gates on
It is a fixed lookup table used for range checks
questions.explanation: Instance columns represent public inputs/outputs: the verifier fixes them, and the prover must match them.

questions.question: In the witness layout, why do we add copy constraints between a@row0 and a@row2 (and similarly for b)?
options: To ensure the same logical variable is reused across rows
To make the field modulus smaller for faster proofs
To encode the addition gate using only constants
To prevent selector columns from ever being zero
questions.explanation: Copy constraints tie together cells that should represent the same value even if they appear in different rows.
